description: Zingiber officinale: leafy shoots from an aromatic rhizome.

diseases.name: Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of ginger in the rainy season.
diseases.causes: Spores spread by rain splash from infected leaves; frequent rain and humidity favour it.
symptoms: Small oval, water-soaked spots on young leaves
Spots turn white to papery in the centre with dark brown borders and yellow halos

steps.title: Remove spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on infected leaves.
Rain splashes spores onto young leaves.

diseases.name: Sheath Blight
diseases.description: A soil-borne fungal blight of the leaf sheaths and leaves of ginger.
diseases.causes: The fungus lives in the soil and infects the lower sheaths in warm, humid weather, especially in dense, wet plantings.
symptoms: Water-soaked, grey-green lesions on the lower leaf sheaths
Lesions become large, irregular and bleached with brown edges
Leaves above the lesions yellow and dry
diseases.effect: Shoots die back, reducing rhizome yield.

steps.title: Remove affected shoots
steps.instruction: Pick off affected shoots when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Improve drainage and spacing
steps.instruction: Avoid waterlogging and thin dense shoots.
steps.rationale: The fungus thrives in wet, crowded conditions.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Rotate crops
prevention.detail: It builds up in the soil.

lifecycle: It infects the lower sheaths in humid weather.
